data.title: Keyframe prompt · 1 · The ping · 0-5s
data.text: Cinematic night shot, a tired startup founder at a kitchen-table desk at 11pm, laptop glow on his face, a Slack notification on screen reading 'Can you send your SOC 2 report?' from a huge enterprise logo. Cold blue light, shallow depth of field.

data.title: Motion + VO · Scene 1
data.text: Slow push-in on his face as the notification pops. His eyes widen, a beat of dread. Camera drifts to the screen. SFX: ping. VO: 'The biggest deal of your life just asked one question.'

data.title: Keyframe prompt · 2 · The old way · 5-10s
data.text: Absurd comedic wide shot: the same founder buried in towers of paper binders, sticky notes and screenshots, a consultant in a suit pointing at an invoice, a wall calendar flipping through months. Warm flat office light, wry tone.

data.title: Motion + VO · Scene 2
data.text: Fast whip-pans between the chaos: pages flying, invoice stamping, calendar pages flipping to 'NINE MONTHS LATER'. VO: 'SOC 2 used to mean spreadsheets, consultants, and a very long year.'

qa.note: Built from the OLDER keyframe (face 0.63). Regenerate from the new keyframe.

data.title: Keyframe prompt · 3 · Enter Comp AI · 10-16s
data.text: Clean macro shot of a laptop screen, the Comp AI app connecting integrations: AWS, GitHub, Okta, Google Workspace as glowing tiles snapping into place. Bright, calm, confident. Founder's relieved face reflected in the screen.

data.title: Motion + VO · Scene 3
data.text: Tiles snap in one by one with checkmark cascades, camera glides across the screen. The mess from scene 2 dissolves away behind. VO: 'Comp AI connects to your stack and does the work for you.'

data.title: Keyframe prompt · 4 · Green across the board · 16-22s
data.text: Hero shot of the Comp AI dashboard, hundreds of controls flipping from red to green, a big compliance score climbing, an auditor's approval stamp landing. Crisp product UI, soft light.

data.title: Motion + VO · Scene 4
data.text: Time-lapse: reds sweeping to green like a wave, score counting up to 100%, a stamp slams down with a satisfying thud. VO: 'Evidence collected. Policies written. Audit-ready, automatically.'

data.title: Video · Scene 4 (v2: light sweeps day to night to dawn)

qa.note: Built from the OLDER keyframe (face 0.57). Regenerate from the new keyframe.

data.title: Keyframe prompt · 5 · The close · 22-27s
data.text: Bright morning, the founder and two teammates around a laptop, an email on screen from the same enterprise logo reading 'Signed.' Everyone erupts in a quiet, real celebration. Golden light through office windows.

data.title: Motion + VO · Scene 5
data.text: Handheld, warm. The founder reads the email, exhales, high-fives a teammate, closes the laptop with a smile. VO: 'Your next deal is a yes.'

data.title: Keyframe prompt · 6 · End card · 27-30s
data.text: Minimal end card: deep dark background, the Comp AI logo centered with a soft emerald glow, tagline 'SOC 2, handled.' in clean white type, trycomp.ai underneath.

data.title: Motion + VO · Scene 6
data.text: Logo resolves out of the last frame's light, tagline fades in, subtle glow pulse. VO: 'Comp AI. SOC 2, handled.'

qa.note: Built from the OLDER keyframe (face 0.59). Regenerate from the new keyframe.

story.title: The Ministry
story.logline: Henrick takes a founder to get SOC 2 the European way. It takes eleven years. Then Comp AI does it in six seconds, and Henrick has to say the word.

sections.name: Payoff

sections.name: Call to action
sections.purpose: The binder goes in the bin. One line, one logo.

open: Founder and Clerk need character sheets too (same one-pass sheet method) before any keyframes.
Scene 6 and the 'It is good' line are real Henrick footage. Scene 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 lines need lip-sync or his cloned voice: his sign-off on the clone is still outstanding.
Keep the Ministry fictional. No real regulators, agencies or flags. Parody a type of bureaucracy, not a country's institution.
40s is long for a social cut. Cut 15s version: scenes 1, 2 (ticket gag), 5, 6, 7.

activity.text: Live activity feed is on. I'll post here as I work.
Auditing all 7 clips frame by frame with the av-review card (not 3 frames per clip).
Audit done. Scene 3 FAIL (clerk turns away, leaves frame), scene 5 FAIL (ends worried, not relieved), scene 4 borderline (too static). Rerolling 3 (x2), 4, 5.
Setting up Remotion (motion graphics): ministry sign, ticket display, form stamp, calendar flip, dashboard score, captions, end card.
Remotion compositions written (7). Rendering transparent overlays now.
Reroll clips for scenes 3 (x2), 4, 5 downloaded; auditing them.
Scene 4 and 5 rerolls pass the audit and are on the board. Scene 3 still fails twice (clerk turns away); changing the shot to a straight-on view of her.
Scene 3: new straight-on keyframe done; 2 Kling attempts rendering.
Motion graphics: moved the form (was covering a face) and the calendar title; re-rendered.
Scene 3 fixed (clerk holds eye contact, 100% face). Assembled rough cut v2 with motion graphics + end card.
Rough cut v2 is on the board: all 7 scenes passed audit, motion graphics composited, end card appended.
Pushed to GitHub: audit fixes, motion graphics, assembly script.
Building a distinct FINAL CUT player and showing the rendered motion graphics on their nodes. Then voices + sound.
Voices: building Henrick clone from his 4 real isolated lines (Index TTS 2); casting founder, clerk, narrator on ElevenLabs v3.

Voices done: Henrick cloned from his real lines (0.76-0.85 match, real-vs-real is 0.71), founder/clerk/narrator cast. All 14 lines pass speech-to-text. Dialogue does not fit current shot lengths, so regenerating scene 1 (new Henrick close-up), scene 3 (10s) and scene 6 (7s) to carry lip-sync.

Seedance 2.5 test: accepts real-face reference images and a voice reference. Face held 100%, voice matched Henrick at 0.86 (best of all methods), lips move on each word. Flaws: dropped the first word, long freezes in pauses, 480p draft. This is the lead approach.
Status: voices done and verified, Seedance is the lead for speaking shots. Next: real-resolution Seedance runs for dialogue shots, sound design, mix with -14 LUFS, assemble final cut v3 with audio.
Resemblance push: building a face-similarity scorer (ArcFace) calibrated on real Henrick footage, then optimizing face and voice against it.

Resemblance baseline measured with ArcFace: real-vs-real 0.82; our keyframes 0.36-0.67, Kling clips 0.46-0.63, Seedance test 0.67. Testing three video-edit face replacements (Genjutsu, Kling Omni Edit, Seedance edit) on the weakest clip, plus full-res Seedance dialogue runs.

Breakthrough: editing a single real still keeps the face at 0.80-0.82 (equals real-vs-real 0.82); generating from my sheet scored 0.67-0.72. Switching every Henrick keyframe to the edit method; 6 new candidates (scenes 2, 4, 6, 7) rendering, scored by ArcFace.

Seedance 1080p: face 0.76 on video, voice 0.86, lips move on every word, but it mangled the two-line prompt (dropped Friday, 4s gap). Now generating each line as its own 1080p clip from the 0.82 edited keyframe (Friday, In Europe..., scene 6 line, scene 7 line). Face-replacement tools (Kling edit, Seedance edit) did NOT help: 0.44-0.45 vs 0.46.

All three video face-replacement tools failed (Genjutsu 0.46, Kling edit 0.45, Seedance edit 0.44; original 0.46). Fix the face at generation time instead. New edit-based keyframes on the board: scene 2 0.70, scene 4 0.77, scene 6 0.78, scene 7 0.76 (old: 0.63, 0.57, 0.50, 0.36). Older clips now flagged to regenerate.
Sound: building the full mix now (dialogue + ambience + effects, -14 LUFS), cut v3 with audio. Not waiting on the remaining clips.
SFX and ambience generated (13 files, ElevenLabs; recorded samples can replace them later). Building the mix script.

Seedance single-line clips PASS: Friday (face 0.82, words exact), In Europe... (face 0.81, voice 0.85), scene 6 line (face 0.77, voice 0.85). Rendering: It is good, scene 4 and scene 2 from the new keyframes, scene 7 retry.

BLOCKER: Higgsfield credits are nearly gone (12.15). Two Seedance jobs rejected; two already-accepted ones still finish. fal has Seedance 2.5 but its account is named Leap, so I am not spending there without Claudio's OK. Continuing with free work: mix, cut, audits.
Cut v3 first audit: -13.7 LUFS, no clipping. Found scene 3 was still the 4.5s clip (9s of dialogue overran into scenes 4-5). Swapped in the 10s clerk clip; rebuilding.
Seedance scene 6 'It is good' (face 0.78) and scene 7 statement (face 0.77) pass with exact words. Rebuilt cut v3 with them.

Final cut v3 is on the board with sound: all lines pass the speech check, -13.8 LUFS. Honest status: not publishable yet. Missing lip-sync on founder and clerk shots, scenes 2 and 4 on older low-resemblance clips, cut runs long. Needs credits (Higgsfield top-up or OK to use fal) to finish.
